summary: SL-089 was a seam-proving slice that changed no shipped code. It added a passive `rows` mode to the window hook, window cases N-005 (SMB), N-006 (cloud, three endings), T-009 (held folder), W-001 (panel vs engine record with an open oracle and its own controls) and R-002 steps f/g, plus Core.Tests twins and plant rows. C1, C2 and C4 were proven on this PC. C3 (whole C:\) passed validate only on bounded roots; the full-drive run is a person's, because of the 0.5 GB pool guard and SL-095's measured ~537 MB cold-scan growth. The slice took 7 reruns of its gates. Three were halts for outside reasons (a stopped critique, the machine guard, questions waiting on a person). Four were real defects in test infrastructure: the trailing-backslash argv, the census regex, and the plants.json anchors, which cost two full laps.

payload.reason: Reflection on SL-089 from the recorded stages. Criteria 1, 2 and 4 are MET. Criterion 3 (whole C:\) was never discharged and is a person's run.

payload.estimate_error: Sized medium / medium risk with one designer. The size was too small. In its own diff the slice touched the window hook (new mode), StallRig/SmbRig, the CfProvider scenario, five window cases, a launch-quoting helper at 15 sites in two scripts, four Core.Tests files, a twinned rule and 9 plant rows. It ran critique x3, build x4, code-review x5 and validate x3. Treat a slice whose deliverable is test infrastructure as `large`, or budget two extra laps. The risk tier was about right in level and wrong in kind. Nothing shipped could regress. The risk was in machine state (SMB mappings, cloud sync roots, kernel pool, the person's desktop) and in checkers that silently check nothing. Every revoke came from that second class.

learned.lesson: A plant row in eng/rules-harness/plants.json is placed only where its anchor equals a whole stripped source line. A prefix anchor leaves the row PLANT-BROKEN and the harness exits 1, but only validate runs the harness (Q-027). Next slice that adds plant rows: the build must run `harness.py --only <ids>` and see each row print AS-RECORDED. A passing xUnit Fact on the pattern is not evidence the plant rows work.
learned.evidence: Rows F36-F40 and P28-P31 anchored on a prefix of WindowReport.cs:276, so none was ever placed. Build #2's O-021 discharge cited the Fact. Code review passed it on laps 1-4 (code-review #5: 'I passed it' on the first lap). Validate #1 found it with harness exit 1. The fix was nine anchor strings, 102/102 AS-RECORDED, and it cost build #4, code-review #5 and validate #3.

learned.lesson: Any case that launches the exe with a root must build its command line through Format-AppArgument (tests/window/WindowCases.ps1; HookCases.ps1 loads it by name). A root ending in a backslash, such as the criterion's `C:\`, otherwise reaches argv as `C:" --report <file>`, report mode never starts, and the case holds a window open for its full timeout. The raw-array cases C-007, C-012 and C-014 bypass the helper on purpose. The guard census (AppArgumentTests.cs:22) catches only backtick-escaped hand-quoting, so a doubled-quote, concatenated or earlier-variable launch line still passes (SC-135). Do not rely on the census; use the helper.
learned.evidence: Code review #1 measured CommandLineToArgvW and a 20 s launch: `C:\Windows\Logs` exits 0 with a report, `C:\Windows\Logs\` never exits. The fix is corpus tests/window/AppArgumentCorpus.json (10 roots, 8 plant lines). The same review showed that `Start-App """$root"" --report ...` passes the census. Code review also noted that from cmd.exe `-Root "C:\"` arrives as `C:"` and Test-W001 stops with 'is not a folder'.

learned.lesson: On this Windows 11 26200 build the cloud half of C1 has no positive control. A CfExecute failure completion (STATUS_CLOUD_FILE_UNSUCCESSFUL), a provider kill and the 60.4 s cldflt timeout all end in a Completed scan with an empty listing and no row for the stalled folder. The only cloud error code ever recorded is 363, from stuck-placeholder teardown leftovers. N-006 therefore reports 'held: platform gives no failed read (Q-177)'. Never describe it as a passed positive check. A slice that wants a cloud-failure control needs a new ending or a real provider.
learned.evidence: N-006 controls (release, kill, timeout) each reported 711 files, 5 folders, 71,100 bytes and no row for s, t or u (O-001, O-002, O-008, validate #1). The cloud-hang spike had already measured kill and timeout at 0/6 controls. Test-N006 fails on a row for s only under the kill and timeout endings; under release such a row becomes the positive control.

learned.lesson: When a done-when names a whole-drive run (here 'whole C:\ scan ... non-elevated'), check at division time whether the engine may run it. Here it may not: the machine guard reads a whole-machine pool counter against 0.5 GB per run, and SL-095 measured ~537 MB for one cold C: scan. Mark such a criterion `checked_by: person` up front. In SL-089 the engine only learned this in critique M8, and the criterion ended as 'not reached' at validate.
learned.evidence: Q-176 let W-001 run unattended on the basis that 'the app only reads'. Critique M8 (accepted) reversed that for W-001 only. W-001 now takes a mandatory -Root and ran on three bounded roots with about +2 MB pool. Obligations list: criteria 1, 2 and 4 are [MET] and 3 is not.

learned.lesson: The engine's kernel-memory guard counts the whole machine, and overlapping acting runs trip it. Run one rig or whole-drive case at a time. N-006 as first built (four rig runs in sequence, the timeout control waiting ~121 s to cldflt's second timeout) took ~7 min. It now runs the four side by side on separate roots and ends the timeout control at the first filter timeout (60.4 s), so the case takes 70 s. The record does not say which run caused the growth in build #1.
learned.evidence: Build #1 halted: kernel memory grew 0.56 GB while run 2572 was running, with 2 acting runs overlapping, past the 0.5 GB limit. Build #2 restructured N-006: 70 s, 4 roots removed, base folder gone. The kill and release mutations each still fail the case.

learned.lesson: The design stage did not read the harness it extends. 9 of the first critique's 16 findings were major. At least five were 'the design contradicts a contract of an existing harness': the hook's fixed mode list (StartupHook.cs:197-200, :278), rules-parity's allowed twinned keys (eng/rules-parity.ps1:344,450), Kill-StallRig leaving the mapping (WindowCases.ps1:666-671), the UnreadableKind enum names, and a two-line fluent layout in WindowReport.cs. The composer also saw only the first 20,000 characters of the single proposal. For the next test-infrastructure slice, put the hook mode list, the rules-parity twinned-key set and the rig kill/teardown semantics in the design brief, and size the critique as the first real review.
learned.evidence: Critique #2 filed 16 findings. Those answered by model: M1 (no passive mode), M2 (OpenRefused vs NothingListed), M3/m1 (rule 2 un-twinnable and redundant), M4, M5, M6, M7 (Q-177 predates the design), M8 (Q-176 vs SL-095). Design note: 'proposal text was clipped at 20,000 characters ... anything after prior_art was not seen'.

learned.lesson: In engine shells %TEMP% is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, which is hostile to cases: Remove-Item is refused there, and the 3 back-dating tests (Q-190) fail. New window cases that create trees must root under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. N-006's roots are in LOCALAPPDATA\Temp\fsa-window-cloud, and Complete-CloudSeamRun deletes with a FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT fallback and asserts NOT-REGISTERED. A stop-seam tree with folders queued after the held one left stuck placeholders (363) in 4 of 6 spike runs. Those leftovers become 363 rows in later C: scans (the ~30 expected rows in criterion 3).
learned.evidence: Reveal spike: Remove-Item 'Access denied' in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, [IO.Directory]::Delete worked. Cloud-hang spike 'zz' tree: 4 of 6 teardowns left placeholders ('cloud file metadata is corrupt'). Critique M6 and O-023. Default suite is 559/562 with the same 3 Q-190 failures before and after SL-089.

learned.lesson: W-001's checker pattern is settled. It opens only code-5 NothingListed rows, with the scanner's plain mask and no listing. It exempts and tallies rows whose CreationTime or ChangeTime is after scan start, and tallies 363, reparse and other codes without opening them. It is inconclusive unless three controls behave: C:\Windows opens, a planted deny-ListDirectory folder gives 5, and a planted deny-WriteAttributes folder gives keep 5 and plain 0. Extend tests/window/W001OracleCorpus.json (15 rows, F01-F15) when changing it. Do not patch the script alone.
learned.evidence: O-026 and O-029; W001OracleTests pass the corpus. The pre-m3 oracle failed F03, F04, F06, F07, F09 and F10 as leaks. W-001 on WER gave 446 rows = header = core.unreadable, all 446 still refused, 7 drawn.

learned.lesson: Validate attempt 3 re-ran no real-contact case and rests on attempt 1's runs at f9c303e. This is sound only because the single later change was plants.json anchors. Any later change under src/, tests/window/ or the rig sources invalidates N-005, N-006, T-009, R-002 f/g and W-001 as evidence and needs a fresh run. Q-176 lets build and validate run them unattended, one at a time, with leftover state failing the case.
learned.evidence: Validate #3: 'git diff --name-only f9c303e HEAD' shows only eng/rules-harness/plants.json; contact is `code`. Attempt 1 left only the person's own Z: mapping and no app, rig, provider or consent process.

candidates.title: Owner runs W-001 over whole C:\ to discharge SL-089 criterion 3
candidates.why: Done-when 3 (panel rows = engine failed-folder count on a non-elevated whole-C:\ scan, no refused-then-listed folder as a row, no empty reason) is the only SL-089 criterion not marked MET. Validate #3 lists it as 'not reached: a person's to run'. Test-W001 in tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 refuses to run unattended on C:\ (critique M8) because SL-095 measured ~537 MB of pool for a cold scan against the 0.5 GB guard. It has run only on bounded roots: WER 446 rows, Windows\Logs 1 row, fsa-guard-tests 27 code-363 rows, and ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows 457 rows, where the notScanned branch ran once. A whole-drive run should give about 682-684 rows (U-098/U-111: 652 code 5, 28 code 363, 2 code 1920) beside ~306,000 refused-then-listed folders that must not be rows. Use the command in docs/design/SL-089-seams.md with the wcifs-layer-store precaution on. Run it from pwsh as `-Root C:\`, not cmd.exe `-Root "C:\"`, which arrives as `C:"`. The result is .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json (counts only). A leaked row's path appears only in the console 'LEAK:' line, because Invoke-WithHook deletes the hook log.

candidates.title: Check every plants.json anchor against its target file in the default suite
candidates.why: eng/rules-harness/plants.json has 102 rows (102 AS-RECORDED at 33ad6f7). harness.py:358-362 places a row only where its anchor equals a whole stripped line of the target file. SL-089's nine rows (F36-F40, P28-P31) anchored on a prefix of WindowReport.cs:276 and were never placed. Four build/review passes missed it, and only validate (the one stage that runs the Python harness, Q-027) found it. The harness needs the engine's Python and cannot run in default `dotnet test` (Q-025). A static Fact in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests, or a step in eng/rules-parity.ps1, could assert that each row's anchor matches exactly one stripped line of its file, so a broken anchor fails at build. plants.json's `_note` also still says no harness run has recorded F36-F40/P28-P31; validate #3 filed that wording fix separately, so it is not repeated here.

candidates.title: Measure whether an unpopulated cloud-placeholder folder whose fetch failed can be told from an empty one
candidates.why: N-006 (tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-N006, provider scenario 'stop-seam' in tests/CfProvider) measured that on this Windows 11 26200 build every ending of a held FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS (CfExecute STATUS_CLOUD_FILE_UNSUCCESSFUL, provider kill, 60.4 s cldflt timeout) gives a Completed scan with 711 files, 5 folders, 71,100 bytes. There is no failed read and no row for s, t or u. Q-177 recorded this as a platform limit and a silent undercount the app cannot detect, and left it unfixed. U-097 and Q-080 saw the same empty-folder shape. Before deciding on any product change, a spike should check whether the placeholder folder's own attributes or reparse state after the listing (still unpopulated vs a genuinely empty directory) differ, using the stop-seam rig. It should also check whether a real provider such as OneDrive ever returns a code (U-110 d: 0 failed rows under a running provider).

missed.what: The design and its 16 findings never asked what argv the app receives for the criterion's own literal root `C:\` when it goes through Invoke-HookedRun/Start-App. The launch line was hand-quoted without doubling a trailing backslash. The app got `C:" --report <file>`, report mode never started, and W-001 would hold a window open for 1200 s. eng/read-window.ps1:52 and CommandLine.RootArgument already encode the rule.
missed.caught_by: code-review #1 (measured CommandLineToArgvW and a 20 s launch of the published exe); fixed in build #3 as Format-AppArgument plus a 10-root corpus

missed.what: Nine plant rows (F36-F40, P28-P31 in eng/rules-harness/plants.json) anchored on a cut-off prefix of WindowReport.cs:276. harness.py:358-362 places a row only on a whole-line match, so none was placed or judged and the harness exited 1. The review passed it on laps 1-4. A check would be to run `harness.py --only F36,P28` and confirm AS-RECORDED, or to assert that each anchor matches exactly one whole stripped line.
missed.caught_by: validate-slice #1 (harness exit 1; the same rows came out 9/9 AS-RECORDED with the full-line anchor)

missed.what: The design named the new held-folder window case T-008. Q-151 already refers to a T-008 (the 0xE0434352 exit launches), so the id was likely taken. The build shipped it as T-009, and the obligations (O-009, O-018) cite T-009. Inferred from Q-151, not from reading WindowCases.ps1: the design never checked the case ids it was allocating.

unknowns: Does a whole-C:\ W-001 run hold on this PC (non-elevated, SL-095 precaution on)? That means rows = core.unreadable = header N, no code-5 row that opens, the header's ', not scanned (M)' suffix parsed on a whole drive, and pool growth inside the 0.5 GB per-run guard. The notScanned branch has only run on C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows.

Can a real cloud provider (OneDrive, or any provider other than tests/CfProvider) make cldflt return an error for a folder listing? Q-177's platform-limit verdict assumes the three endings are all a real provider can produce, and only tests/CfProvider on Windows 11 26200 was measured.

Is the b-row code 59 from the client-side failpoint FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING=b|3|59 what a real SMB server drop gives through the app? The engine-level spike saw raw 64/121 under Cancel and 59 without Cancel. The app-level case injects 59 and states so. This matches the existing Q-150 on whether a real mid-listing error reaches DirectoryReader as a Win32 code.
what_went_wrong: The plants.json anchor defect cost a whole extra cycle (build #4, code-review #5, validate #3) for nine anchor strings. Build #2 discharged O-021 on the strength of a Fact that tests the pattern, while the rule's real plant rows had never been placed. Code review passed it four times and said so itself. Validate was the only stage that ran the harness.

The documented owner command `-Root C:\` would not have produced a report: W-001 would have waited its full 1200 s with a window open on the person's desktop. The design, 3 critique rounds and build #2 all missed it, and code review found it by measurement. The fix touched 15 launch sites across WindowCases.ps1 and HookCases.ps1 and added a 10-root corpus.

The fix's own guard was unsound when first written. The AppArgumentTests census (AppArgumentTests.cs:22) matches only backtick-escaped quotes, so doubled-quote, concatenated and earlier-variable hand-quoting pass it (code-review m2). That is the same 'checker passes without the thing it names' pattern the project has hit before. It was waived to SC-135, so the guard stays partial.

The design was a single proposal, clipped at 20,000 characters when handed to composition, and written before Q-176 and Q-177. The critique did the design's work: 16 findings, 9 major. They included a hook that does nothing without a stop mode, an un-twinnable rule 2, a kill that leaves an SMB mapping, a cloud release that cannot light its control, and an unattended C:\ scan that Q-176's own basis excludes.

A large share of the pass counts is waiting, not rework. Critique #1 was stopped by a person, critique #2 left 16 findings waiting, and design #1 and build-check #1 halted on open questions or a partial survey. Those were answered by a model while the owner was away and are counted as untriaged in the gates' precision. Build #1 was halted by the machine guard (kernel +0.56 GB, two acting runs overlapping). The record does not say which run grew the pool, so the cause is unattributed.

Criterion 3 was not discharged. Validate passed with 3 of 4 criteria MET and C3 carried as 'a person's run'. Validate #3 also re-ran no real-contact case and rests on attempt 1's runs at f9c303e. That is defensible because only plants.json changed since, but this slice's real-contact proof is one lap old.

Build commit f9c303e stopped tracking the 45 `.taad-scratch/` files that SL-095's merge had committed, and neither the builder's account nor its declared deviations mention it. Merging SL-089 removes them from uat. Their copies under docs/design/SL-095-runs/ stay, and no SL-095 record cites a `.taad-scratch` path.
